aiProposal.classification: Contract liability/customer advances; no August revenue.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 proposal: Classify the €90,000 September receipts as contract liabilities, not August revenue. Challenge: A cash receipt could be viewed as revenue if collection is the company's normal trigger.
decisions.studentReasoning: The bank records show €60,000 and €30,000 received in August, but NB-SEP and FF-SEP state delivery dates of 15 and 24 September and confirm that nothing had been delivered by 31 August. I therefore treat the €90,000 as customer advances: cash has arrived, but the performance obligations are still unsatisfied, so there is a liability rather than August revenue.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 proposal: Classify the €50,000 new bank advance as debt and financing cash inflow, not strategic income. Challenge: Management labelled the advance strategic income.

decisions.question: Classify Damaged stock.

answer.classification: Inventory impairment to nil plus disposal provision.

aiProposal.classification: Inventory impairment to nil plus disposal provision.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 proposal: Recognize a €22,000 inventory write-down expense and reduce inventory to exclude the unsaleable stock. Challenge: Management argued physical existence supports carrying value.
decisions.studentReasoning: The 31 August count says the €22,000 basement stock was wet and could not be sold, and the independent assessment confirms no saleable value, so I write the inventory down to nil. For the separate €2,000 provision, my selected case explicitly assumes DPI already had a present legal or constructive removal obligation at 31 August under its warehouse/site responsibilities. The files establish the condition and estimated cost but do not document the source of that obligation, so I also show the no-provision alternative.

alternativeTreatment.assumption: Selected case assumes a present legal or constructive obligation to remove the wet, unsaleable stock existed at 31 August under DPI’s warehouse/site responsibilities. The case files do not document the legal or constructive source, so this is an explicit assumption rather than an evidenced fact.
alternativeTreatment.treatment: If no present obligation existed at 31 August, recognize no €2,000 provision. Recognize the removal cost when the disposal service is received.

decisions.question: Estimate Damaged inventory write-off and document the basis.

answer.basis: Damaged stock is unsaleable and has no recoverable value; independent removal quote is €2,000.

aiProposal.basis: Damaged stock is unsaleable and has no recoverable value; independent removal quote is €2,000.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 proposal: Estimate the damaged-inventory write-off at €22,000, its full carrying amount, because it has no saleable value. Challenge: The €2,000 disposal quote could imply a €24,000 loss or negative inventory value.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 proposal: Do not use management's €312,000 profit for an earn-out. Use the corrected €65,000 base case, with a disclosed €60,000-€79,000 sensitivity and contractual protection for unresolved items. Challenge: The takeover deck's €312,000 might be contractually convenient for the earn-out.
decisions.studentReasoning: Management’s €312,000 profit includes September deposits and a €50,000 bank loan as income and omits supported adjustments, so it is not a reliable earn-out base. I select the reconciled €72,000 case, disclose Agent 2’s €65,000 inventory-based case and the wider sensitivity range, and require contractual protection for the unresolved items.

reconciliations.name: Inventory to physical count after impairment

uncertainties.assessment: Selected base €121,000 from report-date physical saleable stock. Agent 2 roll-forward alternative is €112,000; €9,000 remains a visible count variance.

Selected base recognizes a €2,000 provision only on the explicit assumption that a present legal or constructive removal obligation existed at 31 August. The files show expected cost but do not document the source of an obligation. Without that obligation, no provision is recognized: profit is €74,000, liabilities €406,000 and equity €134,000.
Recognition is strongly supported. Best estimate is €25,000 within counsel’s €20,000-€30,000 range.
No policy, invoice, payment, prepayment, or consumption evidence is supplied. Exposure cannot be quantified.
The €24,000 independent schedule is supplied, but useful lives and residual values are absent.
The €231,000 combined Jan-Aug payment reconciles, but month-specific amounts are not supported.
Selected base is €72,000. Inventory, disposal, and legal alternatives support an indicative €58,000-€79,000 range before unquantified insurance.

boardRecommendation.workingCapitalAndSolvencyWarning: Cash is €60,000 against €408,000 of recognized liabilities, including €126,000 supplier payables and €90,000 of customer deposits funding future delivery. Loan maturity is not supplied, so current/non-current classification remains unresolved.

disposalProvisionAlternative.assumption: Selected case assumes a present legal or constructive obligation to remove the wet, unsaleable stock existed at 31 August under DPI’s warehouse/site responsibilities. disposalProvisionAlternative.treatment: If no present obligation existed at 31 August, recognize no €2,000 provision. Recognize the removal cost when the disposal service is received.

independentAnalyses.comparison: Both agents agree on revenue, cash, receivables, PPE, debt, payroll, legal provision, and owner distributions. The principal disagreement is the €9,000 inventory count variance and whether the €2,000 disposal quote creates a provision.
